item.label: BOOK_02 §02.34a

record.notes: For any finite simple rational adjacency matrix A on 33 vertices with rank at most three and trace(A*A)=718, the full adjacency relation is recovered as a complete three-part partition whose fibre-size multiset is {9;11;13}. No partition, triangle, connectedness or absence of isolated vertices is assumed. Equality of recovered parts is exactly equality of adjacency rows. The third moment 7722 is derived, not supplied. The proof combines a kernel-checked classical rank/clique recognition argument with Turan density bounds and the existing exact vertex/edge inverse theorem; it includes an actual graph isomorphism and a kernel-checked instance of the input passport. Independent exact Python controls include all labelled simple graphs through six vertices and deletion rivals for each of the three readings. The rank-deletion rival K(12;12;9) with one cross-edge removed even preserves the cubic moment. This removes the preselected complete-tripartite class from scene recognition; it does not derive the input readings or the simple-graph operator contract from primitive verifiability, and makes no empirical or classical-theorem novelty claim.
